name: Google (Gmail, Drive, Calendar)

verdict.headline: Your scope tier sets the wait: non-sensitive scopes clear in minutes to 2–3 business days, sensitive scopes (gmail.send, Calendar) take 3–10 business days of review, and restricted scopes (Gmail read, mail.google.com, broad Drive) take about 6 weeks plus a CASA security assessment you pay for and renew every year.
verdict.nextAction: On Data Access, map each feature to the narrowest scope (for example gmail.send instead of https://mail.google.com/) to see which tier you are in, and keep dev and prod in separate Cloud projects.

steps.title: Create or select a Google Cloud project and enable the APIs
steps.detail: Enable the APIs you need (Gmail, Drive, Calendar). You must be a project Owner or Editor.

steps.title: Map features to the narrowest scopes and draft scope justifications
steps.detail: For each scope, write why the app needs it and why narrower scopes fail. Send-only apps should use gmail.send (sensitive) rather than https://mail.google.com/ (restricted).

steps.title: Draft the privacy policy and homepage copy, then audit links and domain match
steps.detail: The homepage must describe the app, and the privacy policy must sit on the same domain with the identical URL on the homepage and consent screen.

steps.title: Create the branding and choose an audience
steps.detail: Menu → Google Auth platform → Branding → Get Started. Enter the app name and user support email, choose Internal or External, add contact email(s), and accept the User Data Policy. Once created, the consent screen can't be removed.

steps.title: Add branding details and verify authorized domains
steps.detail: On Branding, add the homepage, privacy policy, terms and logo, and list the Authorized domains. Verify each domain in Google Search Console with a project Owner or Editor account.
steps.agentHelp: Audit that homepage and privacy policy URLs and domains match before you enter them.

steps.title: Declare every scope on Data Access
steps.detail: Data Access → Add or Remove Scopes. The Console labels each scope non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted.
steps.agentHelp: Provide the feature-to-scope map with the narrowest alternative for each.

steps.title: Add test users
steps.detail: Audience → Test users. External apps only, maximum 100.

steps.title: Create an OAuth client ID
steps.detail: On Clients, create a client (web, desktop and so on) with redirect URIs. Exact field names were not checked.

steps.title: Write the demo-video script and submission checklist
steps.detail: The script must cover the full OAuth flow, the consent screen with the app name and exact scopes, the client ID in the address bar, and each scope in use.

steps.title: Record the demo video and upload it to YouTube as Unlisted
steps.detail: Recorded in English. If data is used for AI training, show the user's explicit consent.
steps.agentHelp: Prepare the shot-by-shot script and a checklist of what must be visible.

steps.title: Verify and publish branding
steps.detail: Click Verify Branding, then publish once the status reads "ready to publish". A compliant result stays valid for only 7 days. If automated verification fails, request a manual review.

steps.title: Publish the app and submit for verification
steps.detail: Click Publish app to move to In production. Then open Verification Center → Prepare for verification, add a justification for each scope and the demo video link, and Submit.
steps.agentHelp: Provide the finished scope justifications and checklist to paste in.

steps.title: Google reviews the submission
steps.detail: Brand verification, then sensitive or restricted scope review. All communication is by email to project Owners and Editors and to the support and contact emails.

steps.title: Answer Trust & Safety emails
steps.detail: Each email pauses the review until you reply. Reply directly to the last email from the verification team.

steps.title: Restricted only: pre-check the CASA self-scan setup and remediation
steps.detail: Prepare for the Tier 2 self-scan process before the assessor engagement.

steps.title: Restricted only: contract and pay a CASA assessor
steps.detail: Once the other requirements pass, Trust & Safety emails you to begin CASA. Use a Google-empanelled assessor (App Defense Alliance framework, based on OWASP ASVS) at AL1 or AL2, and sign off on the results. Passing produces a Letter of Validation/Assessment. Google charges no fee; you pay the assessor.
steps.agentHelp: Pre-check the self-scan setup and remediation.

steps.title: Restricted only: renew every 12 months
steps.detail: The CASA assessment and restricted-scope approval need annual recertification. Adding a new restricted scope may trigger reassessment.

submissionChecklist.detail: Use the narrowest scopes possible, with a written explanation of why narrower scopes fail.

Shows the full OAuth flow, the consent screen with the app name and exact scopes, the client ID in the address bar, and each scope in use. If data is used for AI training, shows the user's explicit consent.
No ads, no selling data, no credit decisions, and human reading only in narrow cases. Using Google user data to train foundational AI models is prohibited.

submissionChecklist.item: Restricted only: CASA Letter of Validation/Assessment
submissionChecklist.detail: From a Google-empanelled assessor at AL1 or AL2, requested by Trust & Safety as the final step.

gotchas.title: Google gives two different sensitive-scope review times
gotchas.detail: The FAQ says 10 business days and the developer page says 3–5. Quote both.

gotchas.title: Testing-mode refresh tokens die after 7 days
gotchas.detail: This looks like a random auth bug.

gotchas.title: The 100-user cap on unverified apps is per project and permanent
gotchas.detail: Keep dev and prod in separate projects and submit only prod. Remove OAuth clients that aren't ready for production before you submit.

gotchas.title: Branding is locked during verification
gotchas.detail: It can't be edited while verification is in progress, and changing the logo, name or domains triggers re-verification.

gotchas.title: Brand verification expires after 7 days
gotchas.detail: A compliant brand-verification result stays valid for only 7 days, so publish it promptly.

gotchas.title: https://mail.google.com/ pulls you into restricted review and CASA
gotchas.detail: It is acceptable only if the app needs permanent delete. Send-only apps should use gmail.send, which is sensitive and avoids CASA.

gotchas.title: Google lists no rejection reasons
gotchas.detail: The causes it does name: scopes broader than needed, a homepage or privacy policy mismatch, policy non-compliance, and unresolved critical vulnerabilities, which can lead to API suspension.

gotchas.title: Restricted-scope approval costs money every year
gotchas.detail: CASA must be renewed every 12 months. Google charges no fee, but you pay the assessor; third-party prices were about $540 for Tier 2 and $4,500 for Tier 3 (TAC Security, 2024) and may be stale. Some apps qualify for a free Tier 2 assessment.

gotchas.title: Refresh tokens are capped at 100 per client per Google account
gotchas.detail: When the limit is reached, the oldest token is silently revoked.

gotchas.title: The consent screen can't be removed once created
gotchas.detail: Once you create the branding and consent screen under Google Auth Platform, it stays on the project.
